note mismatch with what is later proved -- Lemma 2 yields \ell_0 \ll \log\Delta, not the asserted \ell_0 \le \log\Delta. 0086-0089 (Corollary): the deduction \Delta \ll N^{6+\epsilon} => \log\Delta \ll \log N \ll N^{1/8} is fine, but it inherits Theorem 1.1/Lemma 1. 0090 (roadmap): fine. 0091-0093: section framing. 0094-0103 (Serre's classification of maximal subgroups): correctly quoted citation ('contained isomorphic' is a typo). 0104 (first three cases excluded for \ell>37; index 2; definition of \epsilon_\ell as quadratic Dirichlet character): correct, cited to Serre 1981. 0105-0110 (Proposition 1: \epsilon_\ell unramified outside N; \ell | a_p when \epsilon_\ell(p)=-1, p not dividing N): correctly quoted, this is the engine of the argument. 0112 (modularity: weight-2 newform of level N attached to E): correct. 0113-0115 (Deligne bound): typo, |a_n| <= d(n) n^{(k-1)/2} not p^{(k-1)/2}; the intended statement is correct. 0116-0119 (Proposition 2: quadratic twist lies in S_k(\Gamma_0(lcm(N,r^2)))): correct for trivial nebentypus (Ono, Web of Modularity). 0120 (f != f'): valid -- if f=f' then a_p=0 for every p with \epsilon_\ell(p)=-1, a set of primes of density 1/2, contradicting Serre's o(x/log x) bound on primes with a_p=0 for non-CM curves. 0121-0122: spacing only. 0123 (second twist to kill bad primes; descent from n to p): the level bound M | 16N^2 follows from Prop 2 with r | 4N_0; 'tilde a_n != tilde a'_n implies (n,N)=1 and a_n != a'_n' is correct since tilde a_n = psi(n)a_n; a_n != a'_n = chi(n)a_n forces a_n != 0; multiplicativity forces some p^k || n with a_{p^k} != a'_{p^k}, and the prime-power recursion (identical for f and f' at p coprime to the level) then forces a_p != a'_p != 0, hence \epsilon_\ell(p) = -1; equation (5) should read \ell <= |a_p| <= 2\sqrt p but is otherwise correct. 0124-0126 (conductor q of \epsilon_\ell satisfies q <= 4N_0): correct, a quadratic character unramified outside N_0 has fundamental-discriminant conductor dividing 4N_0 (8 at the prime 2 is absorbed). 0127-0129 (Lemma 1 statement): the statement to be proved; its hypothesis list does cover the twisted form tilde f used above. 0130: forward reference, fine. 0131-0132 (Rankin-Selberg setup, normalized eigenvalues, Deligne bound (6), Euler product (7)-(8)): standard and correctly stated. 0133 (Proposition 3, residue at s=1): the object with a simple pole is the Rankin-Selberg convolution L(f (x) bar f, s), not the symmetric square (which is entire); the residue formula quoted is the standard one, so the terminology slip is not fatal but is repeated at 0141. 0134-0139 (Polya-Vinogradov, including explicit form |sum_{n<=z} chi(n)| <= 2 sqrt q log q): correctly quoted. 0140-0141 (equation (11)): the two equalities are correct (lambda_f = lambda_{f'} for n <= X, and lambda_{f'}(n) = chi(n) lambda_f(n)); the inequality X <<_f sum |lambda_f(n)|^2 follows from the simple pole via a Tauberian argument, legitimate as an f-dependent statement. 0142 (implied constant may be taken to be 1/r): unjustified as stated -- the Tauberian error term in sum_{n<=X} lambda_f(n)^2 = cX + E(X) is not controlled uniformly in the level, and the argument needs exactly that uniformity since the conclusion asserts X is smaller than a power of the level; a real gap, though phrased as a plausible standard step. 0143-0146 (Hoffstein-Lockhart <f,f> >> N/log N; factors of N cancel, constant << N^epsilon): the cancellation is correct arithmetic given (10) and (12), but Hoffstein-Lockhart is stated for squarefree level whereas the form in play has level M | 16N^2. 0147-0154 (Goldfeld-Hoffstein-Lieman zero-free region; Watkins for non-CM elliptic curves; 'easy to find a constant to modify the proof', N^{(2)} <= N^2, twisting harmless since chi^2=1): a sketch rather than a proof, but plausible and not the fatal defect. 0155-0156: spacing only. 0157 (equation (13)) -- FIRST FAILING STEP: the passage sum_{n<=X} lambda_f(n)^2 chi(n) << sum_{n<=X} n^{2 epsilon} chi(n) replaces lambda_f(n)^2 by the majorant n^{2 epsilon} termwise inside a sum weighted by the sign-changing chi(n); termwise majorization requires a nonnegative weight. Concretely, for n <= X with chi(n) = -1 the definition of X forces lambda_f(n) = 0, so the true summand is 0 while the 'majorant' contributes -n^{2 epsilon}: the right-hand side is not an upper bound at all. The correct honest bound is sum_{n<=X} lambda_f(n)^2 chi(n) = sum_{n<=X, chi(n)=1} lambda_f(n)^2 <= X^{2 epsilon} #{n<=X : chi(n)=1} << X^{1+2 epsilon}, which is vacuous, whereas the Polya-Vinogradov input only bounds sum_{n<=X} n^{2 epsilon} chi(n) << X^{2 epsilon} sqrt q log q. The needed cancellation would have to come from analytic properties of L(f (x) f', s) (which is entire since f != f'), not from a character-sum bound applied to a weight the argument cannot control. 0158 (combining (11) and (13) to get (14), and the parenthetical justification): the stated justification 'chi(n) is nonnegative for n <= X by definition' is false -- the definition of X yields only that lambda_f(n) = 0 whenever chi(n) = -1 and n <= X, not that chi is nonnegative; hence Lemma 1 and with it Theorem 1.1 are not established. The final sentence's deduction of Theorem 1.1 from Lemma 1 plus (5) and Proposition 1 would be valid if Lemma 1 held (n << q^{1/2+eps} << N_0^{1/2+eps}, p <= n, ell <= 2 sqrt p << N_0^{1/4+eps}). 0159 (N_0^2 <= N when all bad reduction is additive): correct, since additive reduction gives ord_p(N) >= 2; the resulting N^{1/8+eps} inherits the defect in Lemma 1. 0160-0163 (Lemma 2 statement, Zywina's argument): statement only. 0164 (proof of Lemma 2): multiplicative reduction gives ord_p(c_4)=0 and n = ord_p(Delta) > 0 correctly; inequality (16) n <= log Delta / log p <= log Delta is false for p = 2 (log 2 < 1), a minor slip that the asymptotic '>>' in the lemma statement absorbs; the Tate-curve fact that ell > n forces a unipotent element of order ell into the image is correctly cited to Serre IV-20, and since the normalizer of a Cartan in PGL_2(F_ell) has order prime to ell for ell > 2, Serre's criterion rules out the remaining exceptional case for ell > 37, giving surjectivity. 0165-0166 (conclusion of Lemma 2): 'ell >= log Delta implies ell > n' needs strictness and fails at p = 2 by the (16) slip; the asymptotic statement of Lemma 2 nevertheless stands. 0168-0190 (bibliography, end of document): no mathematical content. VERDICT: INVALID; the proof of Lemma 1 -- and hence of Theorems 1.1 and 1.2 and the Corollary -- breaks at line 0157, with the earlier uniformity gap at 0142 as a secondary defect. Lemma 2 (lines 0160-0166) is essentially sound up to the p = 2 constant.
